children: U.S. retail sales rose 1.2% in August from July, falling outside a range of Wall Street Journal historical forecasts for the indicator.
Excluding motor vehicles, the Commerce Department reported retail sales rose 1.4% in August from the prior month, outside a range of Journal historical forecasts for the indicator.

For select economic indicators, including the retail sales report, Dow Jones Newswires measures whether a reported statistic falls outside a historical range of Journal forecasting, and if so, by how much. Those forecast ranges are based on an archive of surveys of economists the Journal has conducted over the past decade.

The gauge provides a way to measure the relative volatility of any one particular indicator, compared not just with a contemporary forecast in the days ahead of an indicator's release, but also with its track record surprising forecasters over time.

In the case of August's retail sales, the range of Journal forecasts relative to the actual reported number over that 10-year period was -0.4 percentage point to +0.3 percentage point. For retail sales excluding motor vehicles, the historical range was -0.4 percentage point to +0.3 percentage point.

August's retail sales growth was higher than a Wall Street Journal forecast of a 0.8% increase. Excluding motor vehicles, the Commerce Department said retail sales growth was higher than consensus expectations for a 0.5% increase.
The ranges are made up of the median of historical forecasts that came in lower than the reported number and the median of forecasts that came in higher.
